title: Moving into further or higher education

body.value:
Starting college or a Post-Leaving Certificate (PLC) course is a big step — there's a lot to organise before September comes around.

This page breaks it down into clear steps: choosing your course, applying, sorting out money and accommodation, and getting set up once you start.

• Further Education (FE): PLCs, apprenticeships, vocational training – usually National Framework of Qualifications (NFQ) Levels 5–6
  • Higher Education (HE): Universities, technological universities, institutes of technology – NFQ Levels 6–10 (undergrad and postgrad)

It's important to consider what qualification level you want and whether you might use FE as a stepping stone to HE later.

Undergraduate

  • apply through the Central Applications Office (CAO). This opens every November
  • check entry requirements, points history, and any specific subject requirements
  • consider DARE (disability) or HEAR (socio-economic) schemes if eligible

PLC/FE

Apply directly to the college. This is a good option if you want a year to build skills, improve CAO points, or try a new area.

Postgrad

Apply directly to the college/university (deadlines vary by course).

• Autumn/early Winter: Research courses, attend open days, register for CAO
  • January: CAO closes for normal applications (late applications cost extra)
  • Spring: Interviews for PLCs, CAO Change-of-Mind opens
  • Summer: Offers (Round 1 CAO in August), PLC offers too. Accept place, pay deposit, start looking for accommodation
  • September: Registration, orientation, classes start

• Student Contribution: Around €3,000 per year for undergrads (covered by SUSI grant if eligible)
  • SUSI Grant: Apply early (opens April) — you’ll need PPS numbers, income documents, and course details
  • Budgeting: Don’t forget rent and rent deposit, utilities, Leap Card for travel, food, books, and a bit of social life

• on-campus: Apply as soon as the portal opens (often very competitive)
  • private rental: Watch for scams, always view in person or through a trusted source, get a written lease, and keep proof of your deposit
  • other options: Digs or house share can be cheaper and easier to get

• register with your college: Get your student card and email
  • get a Leap Card: Student version for cheaper travel
  • open a student bank account if you don’t already have one
  • get your timetable sorted and download any college apps for attendance and assignments
Making the most of college life

• attend orientation: it's a great way to meet people and get admin done
  • join a club or society: it's a great way to make friends and try new things
  • use supports: careers office, student union, counselling, academic supports — all included in your fees
  • learn the system: get familiar with deadlines, how exams work, and where to get grinds or help if you need it

• CAO number/offer letter or PLC acceptance
  • PPS Number
  • SUSI grant confirmation (if applicable)
  • proof of address for bank account/landlord
  • rent deposit
  • Student Leap Card
  • student card/enrolment confirmation
  • timetable and module choices sorted
